correctness.rationale: The polynomial is proper of topological degree 2. After rotation its Jacobian is 4|z|²-u²; the critical circle maps to a once-clockwise, star-shaped deltoid. Its regular complement has precisely two regions with four and two zeros, determined at zero and infinity. The square of the Gaussian shear amplitude is Exp(1); integrating the homothetic deltoid inclusion event yields a Rayleigh Laplace transform and the exact angular integral. Strict complete monotonicity follows by differentiating the positive Laplace law. Direct elliptic integral evaluation yields I1=(9E−K)/(3π), I2=2/3; deltoid area 2π and quadratic moment 3π yield the s⁻² and s⁻⁴ coefficients. Taylor remainders are controlled by Rayleigh and exponential moments. checker.py separately corroborates 350 root-count identities and numerical coefficients without standing in for the proof.

value.rationale: The full zero-count distribution is a natural statistic for independent randomness in the perturbation and target, going beyond deterministic maximum valence. Its exact one-dimensional integral, strict all-order monotonicity, sharp elliptic small-noise slope and rational large-noise coefficients form a reusable normalized stochastic planar-harmonic benchmark. The finite-degree model is intrinsically motivated rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; no unsupported application to physical rational lenses is claimed.
